thread:
anika: heads up — p99 host ingress latency increased ~12% after the v3.4.2 runtime deploy. noticed in staging, smallwrite workloads (many short requests).

sam: thanks — any quick numbers or flame?

anika: quick flame snapshot I grabbed locally (short):
```text
28%  runtime_host  [.] parse_request -> parse_headers
18%  runtime_host  [.] tokenize_batch -> token_pool_wait
14%  libc.so       [.] writev (lots of small writes)
10%  grpc          [.] http2_frame_send
30%  other (syscall/idle)
```

jordan: that stack points at tokenizer lock contention + syscall pressure from tiny frames. did anything touch kernel selection or batching in this release?

perf-bot: autotriage: token_pool_wait metric +3.4x vs baseline; kvcache hit-rate unchanged (0.82 -> 0.81).

maria: iirc we flipped a kernel selector change for short sequences in the release candidate — that could alter memory pathing and tokenization behavior.

anika: correct — kernel_selector now prefers "fast_narrow" for seq_len <= 64. also we tightened batching heuristics to reduce tail for medium requests.

sam: two hypotheses: 1) kernel change pushes more on-host work into tokenize path (more locking/allocation) 2) batching window reduction increases number of writev calls -> syscall overhead + grpc framing cost.

jordan: can we microbench? try the ingress bench with a short-seq distribution and the release binary: 
```bash
./bench_ingress --qps 500 --seq-len-dist short --grpc --duration 2m
```

anika: ran it. reproduces when batch_window <= 1ms. if batch_window=5ms the p99 drops back near baseline.

maria: interesting — so the batching change is a strong signal. but why did token_pool_wait spike?

perf-bot: heap profile shows increased mutex hold times in tokenizer when batches are small and actor concurrency high.

jordan: meaning many tiny batches cause many short tokenization runs, each trying to acquire the tokenizer pool. contention + more syscalls -> blocking on writev.

sam: mitigation candidates: a) revert kernel_selector for short seqs b) restore batch_window to 3-5ms but add prefix coalescing in tokenizer to preserve latency c) implement a write coalescer to reduce writev syscalls on host egress.

anika: i prefer b + c as a less invasive change. reverting kernel selector is easy though if we need a hotfix.

maria: +1 for instrumentation: add per-batch tokenization latency histogram and token_pool queue depth metric so we can alert before p99 climbs.

jordan: i'll take the canary rollback if needed. canary plan: roll selector revert to 10% traffic in staging then observe 10 minutes of steady-state. if p99 drops, promote.

sam: also try toggling grpc settings for write aggregation (channel args / HPACK tweaks) as a short experiment. coalescing at app layer might be more reliable.

anika: plan of action: 1) add tokenizer pool metrics + tiny coalescer (PR queued) 2) test batch_window=5ms on canary 10% 3) prepare kernel-selector revert as a safety rollback

jordan: starting canary: deploying batch_window=5ms to 10% at 7060504055. collecting perf + tcpdump.

anika: perf trace path: /tmp/host_flame_7060504057.svg (uploaded).

deploybot: canary 10% triggered by jordan at 7060504055.

maria: I'll add an e2e that simulates many short chat completions (seq<=64) and record p50/p95/p99 across changes.

sam: thanks — also add a microbench that toggles kernel_selector so we can run perf diffs automatically.

jordan: canary looks cleaner at +10min — p99 back within ~2% of baseline. saving traces and will hold for 30m before promoting.

anika: great, i'll merge the coalescer PR and add the tokenizer histograms. follow-up doc in #eng-runtime with perf numbers.

maria: cheers.

perf-bot: note: kvcache eviction rate unchanged; no immediate KV-action needed.

sam: nice. big takeaway — small batching window can regress host-side tokenization due to contention and syscall pressure. coalescing helps.

anika: filing follow-up ticket: PERF-1921 host-ingress-coalesce-tokenizer-batching.

maria: +1

jordan: done. closing loop once prod roll is green. :thumbsup:
